\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ZeroSpace}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Work tape count is bounded by space used]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.k_le_spaceUsed}
\label{Turing.FinTM.k_le_spaceUsed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet, every Boolean input word
$x$, and every time $t\in\mathbb N$, the number of work tapes of $M$ is at most the
total number of distinct work-tape cells visited through step $t$ when $M$ runs on $x$
from its initial configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero space bound forces no work tapes]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.k_eq_zero_of_exists_zero}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.k_eq_zero_of_exists_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.k_le_spaceUsed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $f$ map binary words to
binary words, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every binary input
$x$, $M$ halts with output $f(x)$ at some time while using at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape
cells. If $s(n)=0$ for at least one natural number $n$, then $M$ has zero work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space class collapses when the bound vanishes]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_eq_zero_of_exists_zero}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_eq_zero_of_exists_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.k_eq_zero_of_exists_zero, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and suppose $s(n)=0$ for at least one natural number
$n$. Then the class of languages decidable in space $s$ up to a constant factor equals
the class decidable in space identically zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear and zero space classes]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_id_eq_SPACE_zero}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_id_eq_SPACE_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE_eq_zero_of_exists_zero}
\difficulty{1}
The class of binary languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by
a constant multiple of the input length is equal to the class decidable using space
bounded by a constant multiple of zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive space bounds and their successors]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_succ_of_pos}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_succ_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono, Complexity.SPACE.mono_const}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s(n)>0$ for every $n$. Then the class of
binary languages decidable with space bounded by a constant multiple of $s(n)$ equals
the class decidable with space bounded by a constant multiple of $s(n)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Successor and maximum space bounds]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_succ_eq_max_one}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_succ_eq_max_one}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono, Complexity.SPACE.mono_const}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the class of binary languages
decidable with space bounded by a constant multiple of $s(n)+1$ equals the class
decidable with space bounded by a constant multiple of $\max(1,s(n))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the Pair Encoding on Binary Expansions]
\lean{Turing.pairEncode_bits_inj}
\label{Turing.pairEncode_bits_inj}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode_injective}
\difficulty{4}
For all bit strings $x,y$ and natural numbers $i,j$, the encodings of $x$ paired with
the binary expansion of $i$ and $y$ paired with the binary expansion of $j$ are equal if
and only if $x=y$ and $i=j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Machine that immediately outputs true]
\lean{Complexity.constTrueTM}
\label{Complexity.constTrueTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
There is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with no work tapes and a
single state. On every transition it leaves the input head in place, writes nothing on
work tapes, emits the symbol true, and halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-step constant-true computation]
\lean{Complexity.constTrueTM_computesInTime}
\label{Complexity.constTrueTM_computesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.constTrueTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be the fixed finite Turing machine that always outputs true. For every finite
Boolean input word $x$, there is a space bound such that $M$ halts after exactly one
step on $x$ and its output is the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The universal language uses zero space]
\lean{Complexity.trueLang_mem_SPACE_zero}
\label{Complexity.trueLang_mem_SPACE_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.constTrueTM, Complexity.constTrueTM_computesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
The language consisting of every finite binary word belongs to $\mathrm{SPACE}(s)$ for
the identically zero bound $s(n)=0$: there are a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ and a finite
binary Turing machine that decides this language using at most $c s(n)=0$ work-tape
cells on every input of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-length parity language uses zero space]
\lean{Complexity.evenLang_mem_SPACE_zero}
\label{Complexity.evenLang_mem_SPACE_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.evenLang, Complexity.evenScanTM, Complexity.evenScanTM_decidesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInSpace_zero_of_k_eq_zero}
\difficulty{4}
The language of Boolean strings containing an even number of true bits is decidable with
zero work-tape space: there are a natural-number constant $c$ and a finite Turing
machine such that, on every input $x$, the machine halts with the one-bit output
indicating whether $x$ belongs to that language, using at most $c\cdot 0=0$ work-tape
cells under the stated space measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant output in one step without work tapes]
\lean{Complexity.exists_zeroTape_const_oneStep}
\label{Complexity.exists_zeroTape_const_oneStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.constTrueTM, Complexity.constTrueTM_computesInTime, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
There exists a finite binary Turing machine with no work tapes that, on every binary
input, halts within one step and outputs the single bit $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-tape parity decision]
\lean{Complexity.exists_zeroTape_parity_decider}
\label{Complexity.exists_zeroTape_parity_decider}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.evenLang, Complexity.evenScanTM, Complexity.evenScanTM_decidesInTime, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
There exists a finite Turing machine with no work tapes that, on every Boolean word $x$,
halts within $|x|+1$ steps and outputs $1$ exactly when the number of entries of $x$
equal to $1$ is even, and outputs $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}
